title: Clebsch-Gordan reduction of 1/2 ⊗ 1/2 via singlet/triplet projectors
expression_sketch: On C^2 ⊗ C^2 with ħ = 1 and S_a = (1/2)*sigma_a acting on factor a: sigma1·sigma2 := Sum_{k=1}^{3} sigma_k⊗sigma_k.  Total-spin projectors (Clebsch-Gordan isotypic split): P_0 = (1/4)*(Id⊗Id - sigma1·sigma2),  P_1 = (1/4)*(3*Id⊗Id + sigma1·sigma2).  Equivalently P_0 = (1 - sigma1·sigma2)/4, P_1 = (3 + sigma1·sigma2)/4.  Algebra: P_0 + P_1 = Id⊗Id, P_0*P_1 = 0, P_0**2 = P_0, P_1**2 = P_1.  Action on the CG basis: |1,1> = |uu>, |1,-1> = |dd>, |1,0> = (1/sqrt(2))*(|ud>+|du>), |0,0> = (1/sqrt(2))*(|ud>-|du>); P_1 projects onto span{|1,m|}, P_0 onto |0,0>.  Eigenvalues: sigma1·sigma2 = +1 on the triplet and -3 on the singlet.
latent_structure: Clebsch-Gordan reduction 1/2 ⊗ 1/2 = 0 ⊕ 1 as symmetry-adapted orthogonal projectors built from the invariant bilinear sigma1·sigma2. The four CG kets are an orbit basis of SU(2); the compact object is the pair of isotypic projectors, not a renamed index.

function_domains.sigma: Pauli matrices on C^2 as in ac-t-pauli-completeness.
function_domains.S: Spin operators S = (1/2) sigma on each factor (Wikipedia spin 1/2).
function_domains.P_0: Orthogonal projector onto the total-spin singlet (s=0).
function_domains.P_1: Orthogonal projector onto the total-spin triplet (s=1).

nonzero_conditions.statement: sqrt(2) is the positive real square root, used only in the ket normalization of the m=0 states.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Triplet state, displayed CG kets with 1/sqrt(2)

positivity_conditions.statement: The ket factor 1/sqrt(2) uses the positive square root.
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED

branch_conventions: sqrt denotes the principal nonnegative real square root on (0,oo); only sqrt(2) appears.
source_provenance: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauli_matrices (sigma product / completeness used to build sigma1·sigma2)
Sakurai, Modern Quantum Mechanics, addition of two spin-1/2 angular momenta.

derived_conditions.statement: S_tot^2 = S1^2+S2^2+2 S1·S2 with S_a^2 = (3/4) Id on each factor, so S1·S2 = (1/2)(s(s+1)-3/2) Id on a definite-s subspace.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: standard angular-momentum addition; Wikipedia Total angular momentum quantum number

derived_conditions.statement: Hence sigma1·sigma2 = 4 S1·S2 equals +1 on s=1 and -3 on s=0, which produces the displayed P_0, P_1.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: S = sigma/2 and the eigenvalues of S_tot^2

derived_conditions.statement: P_0,P_1 are polynomials in the commuting SU(2)-invariant sigma1·sigma2, hence they commute with the diagonal SU(2) action.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

derived_conditions.statement: (sigma1·sigma2)^2 = 3 Id⊗Id - 2 sigma1·sigma2 follows from Pauli products and implies P_0**2=P_0 and P_1**2=P_1 over Q.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

public_source: Wikipedia Triplet state CG kets; Clebsch-Gordan coefficients; Sakurai addition of angular momenta
why_not_cse_lgg: The 4x4 matrix of a generic two-spin operator in the uncoupled product basis has no CSE that yields the coupled (s,m) grading. LGG does not invent total-spin projectors or CG coefficients. The representation change is 1/2⊗1/2 → 0⊕1.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide singlet, triplet, Clebsch-Gordan, P_0, P_1, isotypic. Show the uncoupled 4x4 action or the bilinear sigma⊗sigma sum only.
notes: ħ=1 is a source convention, not an extra physical assumption. Distinguishable tensor factors (not identical-particle antisymmetrization) are the CG setting on C^2⊗C^2. The projector identities are algebraic and do not use sqrt except in the optional ket display.
